name: Bootstrap
notes: No hits on Internet Archive advancedsearch, Chronicling America, or web search for a Newark 'Bootstrap' publication 1981-1983. Search engines return unrelated 'Operation Bootstrap' and generic community organizing results, not this title.

name: The Network: The Newsletter of the African-American Institute of Islamic Research
notes: No digitized copies found. Web search for editor Zain A. Abdullah and the African-American Institute of Islamic Research surfaced only his current academic bio, no archive of the newsletter itself. Only known holding is the Schomburg Center (NN-Sc) per the Danky note, not digitized online.

name: Newark Community Union Project News
notes: Found extensive secondary material on NCUP as an organization (Rise Up Newark, SNAC Cooperative, PBS Revolution '67) but no digitized copy of the 'NCUP News' newsletter itself. IA advancedsearch for title:NCUP returned zero results. SNAC record was bot-gated and yielded no repository/collection links.

name: Black New Jersey Magazine
notes: Wikipedia's 'Black history in Atlantic City, New Jersey' confirms the magazine existed (renamed from Black Atlantic City Magazine in 1987, published to 1990) but has no image or link to digitized issues. No IA, Chronicling America, or library digital collection hits.

name: Fotorama
notes: No matches for the River Edge, NJ Black photography magazine. Web search returned only unrelated Black+White/Black Is photography magazines and a Canadian 'Black Ottawa Scene' Fotorama series.

name: The Hiram Star-News
notes: No hits for King Hiram's Craftsmen Center or the Hiram Star-News newsletter from Vauxhall, NJ. Web search returned only unrelated biblical King Hiram and Hiram's Roadstand (Fort Lee restaurant) results. Only known holding is Howard University (DHU), not digitized online. digifind-it.com site search returned no match.

name: Fire II
notes: Web search returns only the original 1926 Harlem Renaissance 'Fire!!' magazine and its modern homages (FIYAH Lit Mag), not the 1975 Trenton, NJ 'Fire II'. No IA or Chronicling America hits.

name: ONI
notes: IA advancedsearch for title:ONI + Newark returned zero results. No web search hits for the International Black Women's Congress or editor Rhashidah Elaine McNeill's Newark newsletter. Known holdings only at Schomburg (NN-Sc) and Wisconsin Historical Society (WHi), not digitized.

name: Hype Hair
notes: Despite being a well-known, still-active title with abundant cover images circulating on Pinterest/Threads/Lipstick Alley, none of those are stable, downloadable archival sources tied to a library/catalog record confirming issue date and Paramus, NJ imprint. IA full-text search returned no matching magazine scans, only unrelated podcast episodes and a lawsuit filing. Declining to attach an unverifiable social-media image as an archival hit.

name: Right On! Focus
notes: Web search surfaces the separate, much larger 'Right On!' teen magazine (Laufer Company, not DS Magazine/Cresskill) and its editor Cynthia Horner, but nothing specific to the 'Right On! Focus' TV-themed spinoff. IA full-text search for the phrase returned 1,254 unrelated hits (VOA broadcasts, podcasts), no actual match. Only known holding is Schomburg (NN-Sc), not digitized.

name: Black Book Connection, Inc. Newsletter
notes: No hits for this West Orange, NJ newsletter. Web search returned unrelated results (Just Us Books, QBR: The Black Book Review in NYC). Only known holding is Wisconsin Historical Society (WHi), not digitized online.

name: Starline
notes: No hits for Starline Publications (rap/rock music magazine, Route 4 East Paramus, editor Mary Anne Cassata). Web search surfaced her general rock-writing career and unrelated titles (Word Up!, Starz band) but no trace of Starline itself. Only known holding is Wisconsin Historical Society (WHi), not digitized.

name: Just for Black Men
notes: Web search confirms publisher John Blassingame's ongoing career in Paramus, NJ Black men's magazines (his later title 'Black Men' launched 1998, and current 'In Black' / Hype Magazine work), but found no trace of 'Just for Black Men' (1996) itself or any digitized issue. Only known holding is Wisconsin Historical Society (WHi), not digitized.
